security_audit.summary: Most static matches are false positives from Python identifiers, documentation, lookup tables, tests, and standard model operations. Confirmed risks include curl option injection, unvalidated thumbnail destinations, photo uploads without explicit consent, and inadequate safeguards for precise private-location identification. The static catalog covers 400 of 486 matches; 86 omitted matches still require manual review before automatic publication. Static review was capped at 400/486 representative findings; omitted static matches are unconfirmed, so automatic publishing stays disabled until manual review.

remediation.suggestion: Manually review the omitted 86 static analyzer matches or reduce bundled generated/vendor/reference content before enabling automatic publication.

remediation.issue: Remote thumbnail values can be interpreted as curl options in scripts/_net.py.
remediation.suggestion: Validate URL schemes and place '--' before the URL argument. Reject option-shaped values and restrict curl protocols.

remediation.issue: Thumbnail downloads accept remote destinations and redirects without public-address restrictions.
remediation.suggestion: Allow only approved HTTPS thumbnail hosts. Validate resolved addresses and every redirect, blocking loopback, private, link-local, and reserved destinations.

remediation.issue: Default intake sends original photos and variants to Baidu and Yandex without an explicit upload consent step.
remediation.suggestion: Default to local processing with --no-rev. Require explicit service-specific consent before uploads, and offer metadata removal and sensitive-content redaction.

remediation.issue: The privacy rule accepts a stated purpose as sufficient to continue precise geolocation of residences or images containing minors.
remediation.suggestion: Separate legitimate-purpose checks from consent and sensitivity checks. Refuse invasive person tracking and limit private-location precision without appropriate authorization.

remediation.issue: The supplied catalog omits 86 repeated or lower-priority static matches.
remediation.suggestion: Complete manual review of the omitted matches before automatic publication. Do not treat these 400 adjudications as coverage of all 486 matches.

content.user_title: Investigate Photo Locations With Verified Evidence
content.value_statement: Photo locations are difficult to establish when metadata is missing or visual clues are ambiguous. Geo-sleuth compares candidates using image analysis, maps, and geometric checks, then reports evidence and uncertainty.
actual_capabilities: Extract photo metadata and OCR text, generate crops, and collect reverse-image search results through an intake workflow.
Record candidates, clues, evidence, and exclusions on a ranked candidate board with evidence-file checks.
Look up calling codes, driving sides, territories, and available regional plate or area-code tables.
Rank satellite cells with CLIP and candidate ground-level images with DINOv2 and SIFT.
Calculate bearings, camera pose, shadow constraints, possible capture times, and terrain skyline comparisons.
Generate annotated evidence images and reports containing alternatives, confidence levels, and unresolved clues.
limitations: Location precision and capture-time estimates depend on visible clues, reference data, and independent verification.
Mapping and search services can lack coverage, change interfaces, require verification, or limit requests.
Full workflows need Python 3.10+, uv, curl, a browser, and optional model downloads with substantial time and disk requirements.
Default reverse search uploads photos to external services; consent controls, thumbnail validation, and private-location safeguards need improvement.

prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner: collect local evidence before choosing a search route.

prompt_templates.prompt: Compare [candidate places] for my public-landmark photo at [photo path]. Record clues on the candidate board and check them against maps. Ask before image uploads.
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate: compare several plausible public locations.

prompt_templates.prompt: For my photo at [photo path], use [verified public location] and [possible dates] to evaluate sun and shadow constraints. Report assumptions and feasible time ranges.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced: investigate capture time after establishing a location.

prompt_templates.title: Verify an Authorized Location Hypothesis

best_practices: Use owned or authorized public-scene photos, start with --no-rev, and approve external uploads only after reviewing privacy implications.
Record each clue and actual output file, then verify precision with independent constraints or stable ground-level features.
Set a search budget and report alternatives, coverage gaps, unresolved clues, and uncertainty.
anti_patterns: Uploading sensitive photos without informed permission or using the workflow to identify private individuals or residences.
Treating similarity scores, editable metadata, or posting times as verified location or capture-time evidence.
Reporting exact coordinates or excluding candidates without sufficient checks and real evidence files.

faq.question: Which assistants can use this skill?
faq.answer: The skill supports Claude, Codex, and Claude Code. Shell access and the documented runtime dependencies are required for script execution.

faq.question: Does the skill upload my photo?
faq.answer: Default intake uploads original photos and variants to Baidu and Yandex. Use --no-rev to skip image uploads; other selected routes may still use network services.

faq.question: Can it always identify an exact location?
faq.answer: No. Results depend on clues and reference coverage. The workflow can report a supported region, alternatives, or missing evidence instead of exact coordinates.

faq.question: Can it determine when a photo was taken?
faq.answer: It can evaluate metadata and sun or shadow constraints. Without reliable dates, location, and measurements, capture-time estimates remain conditional.

faq.question: What setup does it require?
faq.answer: Use Python 3.10+, uv, and curl. Reverse search needs Chrome or Playwright Chromium; image-ranking routes download model weights and install additional dependencies.

faq.question: What remains unresolved in the security review?
faq.answer: Curl argument handling, thumbnail destination checks, upload consent, and private-location safeguards need improvement. Another 86 static matches require manual review.
